headline: MONTAGE GOLD POURS FIRST AT KONÉ — 1,140OZ OPENING POUR PUTS WEST AFRICA'S NEW 300KOZ/YR MINE MORE THAN 1 YEAR AHEAD OF SCHEDULE
snippet: Montage Gold Corp. (TSX: MAU) poured its first gold at the Koné mine in Côte d'Ivoire on September 26, 2026, yielding approximately 1,140 ounces on the opening pour after more than 400,000 tonnes of ore were processed since ore was first introduced to the oxide circuit on September 8. Construction began December 2024 and first gold came more than one year ahead of the original Q2 2027 target — on budget — at a mine designed to produce 300,000+ oz/year over a 16-year mine life.

headline: CENTINELA WORKERS VOTE 98.73% FOR STRIKE — ANTOFAGASTA FACES MANDATORY MEDIATION AT 290KTPA CHILE COPPER MINE
snippet: Workers from two unions at Antofagasta Minerals' Centinela copper mine in northern Chile voted 98.73% in favour of a strike on Monday September 28, rejecting the company's collective contract offer after Antofagasta refused to equalize benefits across union affiliations. The result triggers a mandatory five-day government-led mediation before a legal strike can begin, extendable by five more days by mutual consent. Centinela produces roughly 290,000 tonnes of copper annually and is one of Chile's largest operations.

headline: CHINA ON PACE FOR DECADE-HIGH 1,700T GOLD IMPORTS IN 2026 — SILVER BATTLES CRITICAL $60/OZ SUPPORT AFTER 8% MONTHLY SLIDE
snippet: Heraeus projects China could import roughly 1,700 tonnes of gold in 2026 if August's pace holds — China took in 1,141 tonnes through eight months, 72% more than the same period in 2025 and already above all of 2025's 940-tonne total. Silver, which fell 4.3% on September 28 to $61.53, has lost 8% over the past month, and Heraeus identifies $60/oz as the critical near-term support level whose breach could accelerate the correction.

headline: ESCONDIDA SUPERVISORS BALLOT CLOSES TODAY — WORLD'S LARGEST COPPER MINE FACES STRIKE AFTER UNION REJECTS BHP 14/14 SHIFT DEMAND
snippet: The Sindicato N°2 supervisors and staff union at BHP's Escondida mine — the world's largest copper mine — is holding its strike vote September 28–30 after unanimously rejecting BHP's final contract offer. The key sticking point is a proposed 14-days-on, 14-days-off shift schedule; the union also refused BHP's request to pause talks following a worker's death on site in late September. A yes vote triggers mandatory government mediation before a legal strike can begin, with potential supply disruption at a mine producing roughly 1.2 million tonnes of copper annually.

headline: SOLITARIO RESOURCES CAT CREEK: FIRST HOLES HIT 383M OF CU-MO PORPHYRY — CEO CALLS CC-001, CC-002 'POTENTIAL DISCOVERY HOLES' IN COLORADO
snippet: Solitario Resources Corp. (TSX: SLR) announced September 28 that its first two drill holes at its wholly owned Cat Creek copper-molybdenum project in Colorado intersected a porphyry-style Cu-Mo system over significant core widths. CC-002 returned a 382.9m core length of visible molybdenite and chalcopyrite from 258.1m depth, with a 110.5m chalcopyrite-rich interval near the bottom; CC-001 showed similar mineralisation but with lower copper intensity. Assays are pending, and the CEO described both holes as potential discovery holes of a new Cu-Mo porphyry system open at depth and along strike.

headline: EASTPORT CRITICAL METALS: 110.8M AT 0.43% CU AT NAK-MAIN — 291KM² GRAVITY SURVEY LAUNCHED OVER 30KM UNTESTED BOTSWANA ANOMALY
snippet: Eastport Critical Metals (TSX-V: EVI) released final assay results from Nakalakwana drilling at its Matsitama Copper Project in Botswana, with the headline result of 110.8m at 0.43% Cu from the Nak-Main corridor confirming a 10km structural strike length. The company simultaneously launched a 291km² gravity geophysical survey over the 30km Thole-to-Copper Snake copper-in-soil anomaly — largely undrilled ground that could define the next major target on its 1,845km² licence package.

headline: UEC REPORTS FISCAL 2026 FULL-YEAR RESULTS TODAY — BURKE HOLLOW CASH COST $32/LB AS SPOT STRATEGY AND $794M TREASURY FACE ANNUAL TEST
snippet: Uranium Energy Corp. (NYSE: UEC) released fiscal year 2026 full-year results pre-market on September 29, the first full fiscal year incorporating production from Burke Hollow in Texas — America's largest new greenfield ISR uranium mine in over a decade. Through three quarters, UEC accumulated 276,516 lbs at a Cash Cost of $32.40/lb, held $794M in liquid assets with no debt, and sold physical inventory at a premium to spot — $101/lb in Q2 versus $80.76/lb spot — making full-year production ramp-up economics the key disclosure for the domestic uranium expansion story.

headline: GOLDMINING INC PIVOTS TO ACTIVE DEVELOPER AT MINING FORUM AMERICAS — AMERICAS PORTFOLIO STILL TRADES BELOW NAV WITH FRESH DRILL CATALYSTS
snippet: GoldMining Inc. (NYSE American: GLDG; TSX: GOLD) argued at Mining Forum Americas 2026 that the market has not priced in its shift from passive project holder to active gold-and-copper developer. Management cited a clean balance sheet, portfolio assets across Brazil, Colombia, Peru, Canada and Alaska — including near-term drilling catalysts at San Jorge — and noted the stock still trades below the sum of its parts. The company has analyst coverage from four independent analysts and is positioning itself as a catalyst-driven development story in a senior-gold bull market.

headline: $18B JUNIOR MINING FINANCING IN H1 2026 — CAPITAL FLOWS TO FUNDED DRILL PROGRAMS; CRITICAL-MINERALS RHETORIC WITHOUT WORK PLANS LEFT BEHIND
snippet: An analysis of 2026 junior mining capital markets finds financing hit US$18 billion in the first half alone — a pace on track to shatter full-year records — but the distribution is highly concentrated. Capital is flowing almost exclusively to well-funded, multi-year drill programs run by experienced operators on the TSX Venture, while single-asset projects relying on critical-minerals rhetoric without credible work programs are being left behind in a market that has finally learned to distinguish quality from story.

headline: LITHIUM FLOOR LOOKS FRAGILE AT $18,800/T — EV AND STORAGE BOOM FAILS TO CLEAR SURPLUS AS BRINE PRODUCERS AND SODIUM-ION RISK WEIGH
snippet: Despite 48% growth in battery storage deployments (307 GWh in 2025) and 11.5 million EV sales globally through July 2026, lithium carbonate is trapped at US$18,826/t as a widening supply surplus, cost insulation from brine producers, and the emerging sodium-ion substitution risk overwhelm the demand tailwind. Mineral Resources' Bald Hill and Core Lithium's Finniss have both restarted, adding back supply that was priced out during the 2024–2025 downturn, and the analysis identifies the $18,000/t level as a fragile structural floor rather than a durable one.
